one_line_intent: Disable PCIe ATS (Address Translation Services) on AMD GPUs where 'harvested' silicon or old VBIOS makes ATS unsafe with the IOMMU.

architecture_rationale.claim: Harvested (partly disabled) AMD GPUs need cache initialisation before ATS is enabled; the IOMMU enables ATS before the GPU driver loads, so the only safe option is to not use ATS.

evidence.excerpt: caches on some AMD GPUs must be initialized before ATS is enabled
ATS will be enabled before the driver has had a chance to load and configure the device.

intentional_vs_accidental.claim: The very specific revision+subsystem check for device 0x15d8 (Raven iGPU) is intentional: only certain platforms showed errors, with no root cause.

evidence.excerpt: There is no root cause.  Turn off ATS on these systems to avoid the issue.

intentional_vs_accidental.claim: All Navi10/Navi14 boards lost ATS in 2022 - a deliberate trade of performance for stability after per-revision quirks kept missing units.

evidence.excerpt: The advantages of ATS are not worth it compared to the potential instabilities on harvested boards.

hardware_timing_dependencies.claim: Depends on VBIOS version shipped on each board; some production boards shipped an old VBIOS lacking the init step.

evidence.excerpt: apparently some boards went to production with an older VBIOS that doesn't do it

suspected_workarounds.claim: Hardware/firmware workaround; the Stoney case was exposed (not caused) by an IOMMU flush-queue change.

evidence.excerpt: Note that the commit in the Fixes tag is not buggy; it just uncovers the problem in the hardware by increasing the ATS flush rate.

external_interfaces.claim: Couples the GPU to the IOMMU subsystem: effect is consumed by the IOMMU driver when deciding whether to enable ATS.

compatibility_certification_sensitive.claim: ATS behaviour on Windows was never validated by OEMs, so Linux cannot rely on vendor validation for this feature.

evidence.excerpt: Microsoft never productized ATS on Windows so OEM platforms that were Windows-only didn't always validate ATS.

reasoning.claim: Without it: IOMMU stalls, page faults and GPU hangs, sometimes 'system failure'.

evidence.excerpt: ATS is broken on this hardware and causes IOMMU stalls and system failure.

historical_lessons.claim: Four iterations (2020-2022) of adding one revision at a time before giving up and disabling the whole family - piecemeal quirking of a family bug does not converge.

evidence.excerpt: There are enough VBIOS escapes without the proper workaround that some users still hit this.
